description:
Add an explicit `owner_id: Id` field to the `Space` type in `jmap-chat-types`, mirroring a coordinated normative addition to draft-atwood-jmap-chat-00 §Space (line 655+).

## Spec coordination

Mark (spec author) to add to draft-atwood-jmap-chat-00 §Space the field:

    `ownerId` (String, immutable, server-set):
    : The ChatContact.id of the Space owner. Set by the server at
      creation time to the caller's ChatContact.id. Owner cannot be
      removed via Space/set; transferring ownership is reserved for a
      future Space/transferOwnership method.

This bead's implementation can land BEFORE the spec edit lands (workspace code ahead of spec is acceptable pre-publish), but the bead remains open until both sides are aligned.

## Implementation

Site: crate-jmap-chat-types/src/space.rs (the `Space` struct definition).

Add field:

    /// The ChatContact.id of the Space owner. Set by the server at
    /// creation time to the caller's ChatContact.id. Immutable via
    /// Space/set; owner transfer requires Space/transferOwnership
    /// (not yet specified).
    ///
    /// Per draft-atwood-jmap-chat-00 §Space (with the ownerId field
    /// addition); §Space/set line 1108 ('The owner cannot be removed').
    pub owner_id: Id,

Position: immediately after `id`. Wire field name: `ownerId` (rename_all = camelCase already applies).

Then update the canonical `Space` construction sites in MemoryBackend (crate-jmap-chat-server/src/memory.rs at handle_chat_space_set's create arm) to assign `owner_id` to the caller's principal_id at create time. This requires JMAP-ga0q.1 (foundation principal_id) to be available so the backend can read it; without that, the create arm has nothing to assign.

## Acceptance

  - `Space.owner_id: Id` field exists with the doc comment above.
  - Wire serializes as `ownerId`. Round-trip preservation test added.
  - MemoryBackend's Space create handler reads `Self::principal_id(caller)` and assigns owner_id (using a placeholder synthetic id when principal_id returns None, with a doc note that this 'no-identity' path produces a single-user-mode owner).
  - JMAP-g7wu.2.4.3's owner-protection check on RemoveMember can be implemented against this field (cross-link bead).
  - `cargo test --workspace` clean.
  - `cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings` clean.
  - Note in PLAN.md that owner-transfer is reserved for future spec work.

## Out of scope

  - The actual spec edit (Mark's task).
  - Space/transferOwnership method (future spec, future bead).
  - Multi-owner support (future spec, future bead).
  - Owner-cannot-be-removed enforcement in apply_space_patch — that's part of JMAP-g7wu.2.4.3's re-scoped acceptance.

## Depends on

  JMAP-ga0q.1 (foundation principal_id) — the MemoryBackend create handler needs to read the caller's principal to populate owner_id.
notes:
Keeping the human label intentionally: Mark (spec author) needs to edit draft-atwood-jmap-chat-00 to add the ownerId field to §Space before this bead's implementation lands. Mark, drop the human label once the spec edit is committed (or once you decide to land the chat-types impl ahead of the spec edit per the pre-publish allowance noted in the bead body).
Locked-in design (2026-05-11, Mark): A on all five dimensions.

  1. Field shape: `ownerId` (String, immutable, server-set). Cookie-cutter `<thing>Id` pattern.
  2. Relationship to members: `ownerId` MUST always be present in `members[].id`. Owner is a member; ownership is a tag on top of membership.
  3. Owner permissions: IMPLICIT all-permissions, regardless of roles. Removing roles or revoking permissions cannot demote the owner. Matches Discord/Slack/Mattermost convention.
  4. Owner transfer: reserved for future spec. No transfer mechanism in this draft. `Space/set` has no patch op for `ownerId`.
  5. Cardinality: single owner. `ownerId: Id` (not `Id[]`). Multi-owner is achievable with normal admin permissions.

Optional dimension 6 (broaden to Chat for `kind: "group"`) was NOT picked up. Group-chat ownership remains implicit / under-specified in this draft. If it bites later, file a follow-up bead.

Implementation impact across the workspace:
  - JMAP-g7wu.2.4.11 (this bead): field addition in chat-types + MemoryBackend create-arm assigns it from caller's principal_id.
  - JMAP-g7wu.2.4.3 (re-scoped backend bead): enforces (a) ownerId MUST be in members at all times, (b) implicit all-permissions for ownerId in permission-resolution, (c) RemoveMember on ownerId rejects, (d) Destroy requires caller == ownerId.

Next action for Mark: paste the spec text from the conversation into ~/PROJECT/jmap-chat-spec/draft-atwood-jmap-chat-00.md (four edits: §Space field add, Creating a Space rewrite, removeMembers rewrite, Destroying rewrite). Then drop the 'human' label here; the autonomous loop owns the implementation work.
Dimension 6 confirmed (2026-05-11, Mark): A — do NOT broaden `ownerId` to Chat for `kind: "group"`. The group chat admin/ownership model is genuinely under-specified in the draft and needs proper design work (admins, federation interactions, multi-server enforcement). Premature commitment via half-broadening would lock in a single-creator model that may conflict with the eventual multi-admin design.

Deferred work captured in JMAP-pep4 (filed as follow-up spec-author bead).
Explicit authorization (2026-05-11, Mark): land the chat-types implementation ahead of the spec edit. Per the bead body's pre-publish allowance ('This bead's implementation can land BEFORE the spec edit lands') and the workspace-code-ahead-of-spec norm, the autonomous loop owns the implementation work.

JMAP-ga0q.1 (foundation principal_id) is closed, so the MemoryBackend create-arm has principal_id available to populate Space.owner_id.

Bead stays open until the matching spec edit also lands in draft-atwood-jmap-chat-00 (Mark's task: \u00a7Space field add, \u00a7Creating a Space, \u00a7removeMembers, \u00a7Destroying).
Design reversal (2026-05-12, Mark): the locked-in 5-dimension design captured in the 2026-05-11 NOTES above is SUPERSEDED. The JMAP Chat spec will NOT declare a normative `ownerId` field on `Space`; "who controls a Space" is implementation-defined / out-of-band. Reasoning: keep the wire shape minimal, let deployments choose Discord-shaped (single owner), Matrix-shaped (no irreducible owner), enterprise-shaped (IDP-mediated), or other models.

Closing this bead as SUPERSEDED. The workspace impl that landed in commit cd89717 (the Space.owner_id field, the create-arm assignment, the SPACE_READONLY entry, the PLAN.md "Reserved for future spec work" pointer) must be reverted; tracked as JMAP-g7wu.2.4.12.

The spec edit that this bead was waiting on is no longer just "add the ownerId field" — it is now a broader rewrite of six prose sites that already commit to an owner concept (lines 412, 658, 1069, 1091, 1116, 1409 in draft-atwood-jmap-chat-00.md as of 2026-05-12). Mark will hand a revised prompt to the spec-repo opencode session; that work is tracked in the jmap-chat-spec repo's own bd, not here.

Do not act on the 2026-05-11 "locked-in design" notes above. They are historical context, not current direction.
title: Add ownerId: Id field to Space type + chat-types impl (coordinated with draft spec edit)
